All recent cases of sabotage
which have occurred have been
the work Of individuals. Dis
gruntled employees, workers who
feel that they have not been done
right by and therefore have a
personal grudge to settle with
the boss or the company, have
taken out their spite by damag-
ing plant equipment or its pro-
ducts. But these sabotage at
tempts have not been the tech
nically perfect efforts of organ
lied groups of foreign agents,
operating to destroy or impair
American industrial production
for defense.


Most Of the tricks of the pro-
fessional saboteur are of course
known. They have been catalo-
gued ever since the last war,
and that of course makes IL cas-
Ter now to watch for them, and
prevent them.


There is the old stuff of dam
age to machines by breakage,
manipulation, abrasives, chemi-
calls and so on. The use Of bombs
and incendiaries. Damage to
power stations and power trans
mission line. Damage to raw
materials. Damage to precision
tools. Theft or destruction of
blueprints or specifications.
Damage to lines of communica-
tions and transportation. Pollu-
ton of water supply or of food
supplies. Damage to personnel.
Those lodges are all known and
can be guarded against If not
actually prevented.

But because the police and
protection methods are better
now than they were in the last
war, the saboteur of today has
had to invent new tricks. And
now and then a man will come
up with a strange device that Is
diabolical in it its cunning.


Take the case of the phono-
graph needle that crippled q
